candlestick_engine.title: Japanese Candlestick Recognition Engine
candlestick_engine.summary: Nets 17 candlestick patterns (12 classical + 5 modern Kaabar formations) over a rolling 5-session window into a [-2, +2] score. Open the card for the full catalogue, each pattern linked to a good explanation online.
candlestick_engine.origin: Munehisa Homma (1700s Japanese rice trading), extended with Daniel Chesler's Hikkake and Sofien Kaabar's modern trend-following patterns (Mastering Financial Pattern Recognition, O'Reilly).
candlestick_engine.body:
Scans the last 5 sessions for 17 candlestick patterns and nets their bullish vs. bearish fires into one score in [-2, +2] ((bulls − bears) / 5 × 2, clamped). Bullish clusters tilt the entry score up; bearish clusters pull it down. Twelve are classical Japanese/Western formations; five are modern trend-following patterns coined by Sofien Kaabar. Each name links to a full explanation:

Classical reversal & continuation
  • • Engulfing — the 2nd body fully engulfs the 1st — strong reversal.
  • • Harami — small body contained inside the prior large body; reversal / pause.
  • • Harami (strict) — stricter Harami — the whole small candle sits inside the prior body.
  • • Doji — open ≈ close; indecision, a reversal hinge between two trend candles.
  • • Star (Morning / Evening) — small gapped middle candle between two opposite bodies; reversal.
  • • Piercing / Dark Cloud — gap then a close back through the midpoint of the prior body; reversal.
  • • Tasuki Gap — gap in the trend, then a partial fill that holds; continuation.
  • • Three Methods (Rising / Falling) — 3 small counter-candles inside a big one, then breakout; continuation.
  • • Hikkake — inside-bar false breakout that traps, then reverses (Daniel Chesler).
  • • Tweezers (Top / Bottom) — back-to-back matching highs or lows; minor reversal.
  • • On-Neck — second close returns exactly to the prior close; continuation.
  • • Stick Sandwich — two same-close candles bracketing an opposite one (Bulkowski stats).
Modern trend-following (Sofien Kaabar)
  • • Bottle — trend candle opening flush with its low/high after a gap; momentum.
  • • Double Trouble — a bar whose range exceeds 2× ATR extending the move.
  • • Quintuplets — five consecutive small same-colour bodies; exhaustion/continuation.
  • • Slingshot — breakout, shallow pullback, then re-break in the trend direction.
  • • H Pattern — doji flanked by two same-direction candles forming an 'H'; continuation.

Detectors live in aether/signals.py; aggregation in aether/patterns.py :: candlestick_score().
config: Patterns scanned (17): Engulfing, Harami (+strict), Doji, Piercing, Star, Tasuki Gap, Three Methods, Hikkake, Tweezers, On-Neck, Stick Sandwich, Bottle, Double Trouble, Quintuplets, Slingshot, H.
Lookback: the last 5 sessions; each pattern counts once if it fires anywhere in the window.
Score: net (bullish - bearish) fires, scaled (raw / 5 x 2) and clamped to [-2, +2].
Small-body threshold: 1% of the recent 5-bar average close (gates Tweezers & Quintuplets).
Double Trouble range gate: bar high-low range > 2x the prior ATR.
Source: aether/signals.py detectors + aether/patterns.py::candlestick_score().

split_adjusted_levels.title: Split-Adjusted Level Detection
split_adjusted_levels.summary: Back-adjusts raw unadjusted OHLCV across stock splits before computing swing-low support, swing-high resistance, and ATR stops — so a split inside the lookback can no longer place a level at the wrong price scale. An open-agreement guard preserves real intraday crashes.
split_adjusted_levels.origin: Project AETHER Data-Integrity Gate. Surfaced by the Aug-2026 leveraged / inverse / crypto levels study, where unadjusted pre-split pivots were the dominant cause of that cohort's low backtest win-rate.
split_adjusted_levels.body:
The local OHLCV cache is raw Alpha-Vantage, unadjusted — there is no adjusted-close field. When a stock splits inside the 60-bar pivot lookback or 14-bar ATR window, the pre-split bars sit at ¼× or 4× the current price scale, so swing-low support returns an absurd level, swing-high resistance finds none, and ATR is distorted — a capital-preservation failure (a stop can land far below price, i.e. effectively no stop).

Every unadjusted series is now back-adjusted onto the current scale (cumulative product of detected split ratios) before detect_support / detect_resistance / _atr_from_series and the separate calculate_atr path run. A crash-vs-split guard prevents mistaking a real sell-off for a split: a day-over-day close ratio outside [0.55, 1.8] is only treated as a split when the open moved by ~the same factor. No-split symbols hit a fast path with zero behavior change.
config: Split trigger: day-over-day close ratio ≥ 1.8× or ≤ 0.55×.
Crash guard: confirmed only if |r_open − r_close| ≤ 0.35×r_close (open moved with the close); missing/zero open → left unadjusted.
Back-adjustment: newest bar stays nominal; older bars scaled by the cumulative product of split ratios, keeping the series consistent with the live price.
Applied in: risk_utils._load_ohlcv_series (feeds detect_support/resistance + _atr_from_series) and calculate_atr (live stop distance).
Scope: corrects level/ATR math for every symbol; independent of the leveraged/inverse/crypto exclusion, which remains until its own backtest clears.

Ranking: combined score (desc), then confirmed setup, then reward:risk, then alphabetical; fully deterministic.
Surfaces: Research-page row selection + inline panel, web chat 'compare/vs' intent, console script, /compare-stocks agent skill.

digit_sum_numerology.title: Digit-Sum Numerology Factor
digit_sum_numerology.summary: Status (2026-11-12, R&D #72): failed its out-of-sample test. Rebuilt from pre-2023 data, it didn't improve candidate ranking (IC -0.0008, t -0.61) or the portfolio (t 1.42; 40% of robustness draws). Owner decision (2026-11-24): shadowed. The score is still computed for every stock (digit_sum_raw) but adds nothing to Short10 or Long60, except for stocks on Data/digit_sum_allowlist.json, which a monthly per-stock check writes (scripts/backtesting/digit_sum_per_stock.py: discover on 24 months with Benjamini-Hochberg at 10%, confirm on the next 12). First check (2026-11-24): 114 stocks tested, none confirmed, so the term is off for every stock. Backtested across 522 symbols × 9+ years. Tests whether the digit-sum of a stock's open/close price predicts same-day or next-day direction. Two variants (integer and full-cents) cover 228 unique symbols with 95%+ confidence signals. Of 473 raw signals, 224 pass the full 4-layer quality validator and are active in scoring. Symbol page shows a Stability column: stable / mixed / sparse / flip.
digit_sum_numerology.origin: Inspired by W.D. Gann's numerology research (1878–1955). Empirically backtested by AETHER across 522 symbols × 9+ years of daily OHLCV data (2014–2026).
digit_sum_numerology.body:
Tests whether the digit-sum of a stock's price predicts short-term direction. Digit-sum collapses any price to a single digit: $247.35 → 2+4+7+3+5=21 → 3.

AETHER runs two variants simultaneously:

  • Integer digit-sum — whole-dollar only ($247 → 4). 162/522 symbols with 95%+ signals.
  • Full-cents digit-sum — includes cents ($247.35 → 3). Adds 106 unique symbols not captured by integer-only.

Two timing modes:

  • Prior-close → next-day: standing factor in S10/L60, computed nightly from OHLCV cache.
  • Today's open → same-day: real-time tiebreaker in _execute_buys() using live open price. Logged as 🔢 [Digit-Sum].

Of 473 signals at 95%+ confidence, only 224 pass all four quality gates and are used in scoring. See the Signal Quality Validator wiki entry for the full filter pipeline.

The Symbol detail modal shows a digit table with a Stability column: stable / mixed / sparse / flip / stale.
config: Integer digit-sum OPEN→same-day: real-time only, applied in _execute_buys() at buy time
Integer digit-sum CLOSE→next-day: standing factor, S10 weight ±1.0, L60 weight ±0.5
Full-cents digit-sum: same two modes, combined with integer (averaged when both fire)
Activation gate: |z|≥2.0 (95%+ confidence), N≥50 per bucket

pattern_discovery.title: Pattern Discovery Agent — Missed Winners Retrospective
pattern_discovery.summary: Weekly self-improvement loop: replay a past date, find the top 10 actual winners, diagnose why each was missed, and extract candidate new scoring factors. Two-layer design — a Python computation engine reconstructs 475 symbol scores from the Chaikin cache in ~14s (parallelized), followed by an LLM agent that reasons about why patterns exist and names them. First finding (Jul 2026): lt_trend=Strong penalized -3.0 in L60 appeared in 95% of missed 60-day winners across 3 dates — weight corrected to 0. Runs every Saturday at 10:00 as the AETHER_PatternDiscovery task (replay date: today − 25 days); the analysis is written by AETHER's own AI layer (config ai) and emailed, or skipped and reported when no provider answers. Also run from the System page or via /pattern-discover.
pattern_discovery.origin: AETHER Internal R&D (July 2026). Inspired by W.D. Gann's retrospective analysis approach and Amy Edmondson's Right Kind of Wrong — learning from intelligent failures.
pattern_discovery.body:
A self-improving learning loop that finds stocks the system missed, diagnoses why it missed them, and extracts candidate new scoring factors.

How it works (run weekly on Saturdays):

  1. Historical replay — reconstructs every symbol's AETHER scores as they were on a past date (reads from the Chaikin per-symbol cache, no live API needed).
  2. Forward returns — computes actual 10-day (S10) and 60-day (L60) returns from OHLCV for all symbols.
  3. Classify winners — ranks actual winners; marks each as bought (system selected it), missed (system rejected it despite being in universe), or not in universe.
  4. Diagnose misses — for each missed winner records the exact filter that rejected it (score < threshold, wrong PGR, setup=False) and which factor was most anomalous vs the universe.
  5. Extract patterns — two types: (a) missed-winner patterns: factor combos present in missed winners but penalized in the model; (b) false-positive guards: signals common in stocks the system bought that then lost.
  6. Validate — rolls candidate patterns across 16 historical dates. Only patterns with |z|≥2.0 and N≥30 are promoted to the scoring backlog.

First finding (Jul 2026): lt_trend=Strong appeared in 95% of L60 missed winners across 3 dates. The -3.0 contrarian penalty was excluding exactly the stocks that performed best over 60 days. Weight updated: Strong → 0 (was -3.0) in L60.

Scheduled: the AETHER_PatternDiscovery task (Sat 10:00) replays today − 25 days, sends the report and the skill's analysis steps to AETHER's AI layer, saves the answer as Data/pattern_discovery_{DATE}_ai.md and emails it. If no AI provider answers, the email says why and carries the computed counts; the report stays on disk. It replaced the Gemini CLI agent task, which failed with HTTP 403 on PROD every Saturday from at least 2026-09-19. Run from the System page, or invoke the /pattern-discover skill by hand.

Schedule: AETHER_PatternDiscovery, Sat 10:00, scripts/backtesting/rd_pattern_discovery.py (replay date today − 25 days; --date to pick one)

Output: Data/pattern_discovery_{DATE}.json — machine-readable for the /pattern-discover skill
Weekly cadence: run same date each week; pattern recurring in 3+ weeks = strong validation signal

signal_quality_validator.title: Signal Quality Validator — 4-Layer Filter Pipeline
signal_quality_validator.summary: 4-layer filter pipeline that rejects statistical signals concentrated in the wrong time period, self-contradicting across eras, or from price regimes no longer relevant. Checks: (1) |z|≥2.0 significance, (2) temporal persistence across 6 rolling 2-year windows, (3) no direction flip between eras, (4) adequate coverage at current price level. Reusable framework for all future experimental factors.
signal_quality_validator.origin: AETHER Internal R&D — discovered during temporal distribution audit of digit-sum signals (July 2026).
signal_quality_validator.body:
Before any statistical signal enters the scoring engine, AETHER runs it through a 4-layer quality filter to reject noise masquerading as signal.

The problem discovered: a signal can show z=+2.5 overall yet be completely unreliable — if it fired 700 times when a stock was at $15 and only 30 times at today's $200, or if it was bullish in 2016 and bearish in 2022.

The 4 filters applied in sequence:

  1. Statistical significance — |z| ≥ 2.0 (95%+ confidence) with N ≥ 50 days per bucket. Eliminates weak correlations.
  2. Temporal consistency — Signal is tested across 6 rolling 2-year windows (2014–2026). Must fire in same direction in ≥ 2 windows to be kept; ≥ 4 windows = "stable". Rejects historically-concentrated signals.
  3. Direction stability (has_flip) — If the signal is bullish in some windows and bearish in others, it is rejected. A self-contradicting signal has no predictive value regardless of overall z-score.
  4. Coverage adequacy (is_sparse) — The digit must appear in ≥ 3 of 6 windows (coverage ≥ 50%). Low coverage means the digit barely exists at the stock's current price level — the signal has no recent history to validate.

Result for digit-sum: 473 signals at 95%+ → 224 pass all four gates (53% rejection rate). Each rejected signal is still displayed in the Symbol modal Stability column so you can see exactly why it was downgraded.

This pipeline is reusable — future experimental factors (Gann levels, gap persistence, round-number proximity) will run through the same 4-layer validator before entering the score.
config: Layer 1 — Statistical: |z| ≥ 2.0, N ≥ 50 per bucket
Layer 2 — Temporal: fires in same direction in ≥ 2 of 6 rolling 2-year windows
Layer 3 — Direction: no flip (bullish in some windows, bearish in others) → rejected
Layer 4 — Coverage: digit appears in ≥ 3/6 windows (≥ 50% coverage) → sparse = rejected
Symbol modal Stability badge: stable (4+ windows) | mixed (2-3) | flip | sparse | stale
Scoring engine only loads signals passing layers 2+3+4 — stale/flip/sparse excluded
473 raw digit-sum signals → 224 active after all filters (53% rejection rate)

rbr.title: Rubber-Band Reversal (RBR) — Overreaction Pullback + Fast Recovery
rbr.summary: A positively-signed bullish factor: a big, fast overreaction drawdown (Leg 1) followed by a confirmed higher-low green reversal bar in the upper half of its range (Leg 2). Pure price/volume, no look-ahead — the trough must already be in before the recovery bar scores. The tradeable event is the confirmed recovery bar, not the gap. Backtested on 25+ yr of OHLCV; only the reliable no-gap pocket scores, while the higher-variance earnings-gap cohort is watch-only (RBR↑(gap,watch)). Anchored on INTC's Jul-2026 snap-back.
rbr.origin: AETHER Internal R&D (Aug 2026 lab), anchored on INTC's Jul-2026 earnings gap. Formalizes the AI-age machine/headline-driven overshoot-then-V-recover tape.
rbr.body: A positively-signed BULLISH factor: a big, fast overreaction drawdown (Leg 1) followed by a CONFIRMED higher-low green reversal bar sitting in the upper half of its range (Leg 2). Pure price/volume, no look-ahead — the trough must already be in before the recovery bar scores. The tradeable event is the confirmed recovery bar, not the gap (catching INTC's knife on day one ate another -11% before the bounce). Fed to short_score (+0.5) / long_score (+0.25) through the dedicated vrecovery_score field, never the negated contrarian chart path.
config: Leg 1 depth: <= -10% overreaction floor; <= -15% = the validated deep pocket
Leg 1 speed: trough within <= 8 bars; <= 5 bars = the fast pocket
Leg 2: higher low + green close + close in upper half of range (range_pos >= 0.50)
+2.0 validated no-gap pocket (deep + fast + strong close)
+1.25 near-fast no-gap recovery (one bar outside the pocket)
+1.0 milder confirmed recovery
0.0 earnings-GAP cohort — WATCH-ONLY (tag RBR↑(gap,watch)): win ~0.52, never cleared its own gate, so it is surfaced to watch but carries no buy weight
Shared Leg-1 geometry: patterns.rbr_leg1(); live monitor: scripts/monitoring/rbr_watch.py; parameter sweep recalibrated MONTHLY

profit_lock.title: AETHER Profit-Lock (Trailing Stop Ratchet)
profit_lock.origin: Project AETHER Loss-Minimization core, extending Peter Lynch's 'let winners run' with a mechanical breakeven ratchet (plans/trailing-stop-adjuster.md).
profit_lock.summary: Ratchets the trailing stop upward as a position rallies. Once unrealized profit exceeds 1.0× ATR the stop begins climbing behind price; past 1.5× ATR it locks the stop to the cost basis — a breakeven lock that makes the trade risk-free early in the trend.
profit_lock.body: Dynamically tightens the stop-loss floor upward as an open position moves into profit, so gains are progressively protected without capping the upside. Two rungs, both measured in ATR of unrealized profit above the cost basis: at > 1.0× ATR the stop ratchets up to trail price, and at > 1.5× ATR it jumps to the cost basis (breakeven), so the position can no longer close red. Structural-Scarcity holdings use a tighter 1.5× ATR multiplier; standard satellites use the profile ATR multiplier (2.5×). The stop is only ever moved up, never down.
config: Ratchet rung: unrealized profit > 1.0x ATR -> stop trails up behind price
Breakeven lock: unrealized profit > 1.5x ATR -> stop floor bumped to cost basis
ATR multiplier: 1.5x for Scarcity-core names, else the profile ATR multiplier (2.5x)
Monotonic: the stop is only raised, never lowered
Source: ai_portfolio_game.py profit-lock ratchet (see plans/trailing-stop-adjuster.md)

zero_cash_drag.title: Zero-Cash Drag Autopilot & Fractional Sizing
zero_cash_drag.origin: Project AETHER capital-efficiency core; regime read from get_market_regime() (SPY Long60).
zero_cash_drag.summary: Drops the cash buffer to 0.0% in the AGGRESSIVE market regime (SPY L60 > 2) to fully deploy capital when the broad trend is strong. Pairs with 3-decimal fractional share sizing (e.g. 1.458 shares) on S&P 100 blue chips and core ETFs (DIA, SPY, QQQ, IWM) so almost no cash sits idle.
zero_cash_drag.body: Eliminates the drag of uninvested cash when the market regime justifies it. When get_market_regime() returns AGGRESSIVE — the strong-bull state defined by SPY Long60 > 2 — the required cash buffer is dropped to 0%, so the autopilot can deploy fully. To spend the last sliver of cash instead of leaving a stub, sizing supports fractional shares to 3 decimals (values like 1.458 shares) on S&P 100 blue chips and the core ETFs (DIA, SPY, QQQ, IWM). In weaker regimes the profile's normal cushion still applies (Balanced 20%, Defensive 50%) — zero-drag is specifically the AGGRESSIVE-regime behavior, not a blanket setting.
config: Trigger: market regime == AGGRESSIVE (SPY Long60 > 2)
Effect: required cash buffer dropped to 0.0% for full deployment
Fractional sizing: 3-decimal share quantities (e.g. 1.458) on S&P 100 names + DIA/SPY/QQQ/IWM
Non-aggressive regimes retain their normal cash cushion (Balanced 20%, Defensive 50%)
Source: ai_portfolio_game.py regime/cash-buffer logic + aether/instruments.py fractional sizing

momentum_floor.title: Strict Short10 Momentum Floor (S10 ≥ 2.5)
momentum_floor.origin: AETHER backtrack calibration (scripts/backtesting/backtrack_rules.py) — a single-filter entry gate proven on historical replay.
momentum_floor.summary: Backtest-proven entry filter that strictly blocks buying any setup whose Short-Term entry score (Short10) is < 2.5. Backtracking verifies this single filter avoids ~40% of historically losing trades (including PKX, ETHT, SA), boosting the historical Win Rate from 50.0% to 66.7% and nearly tripling net P&L from +7.75% to +27.88%.
momentum_floor.body: A hard pre-buy gate: on autopilot, any candidate whose Short10 entry score is below 2.5 is rejected outright, regardless of its long-term score or PGR. The threshold was not guessed — backtracking the rule over historical trades showed it filters out roughly 40% of the losers (PKX, ETHT, SA among them) while keeping the winners, lifting the sample win rate from 50.0% to 66.7% and net P&L from +7.75% to +27.88%. It enforces the discipline of never buying weak short-term momentum just because the long-term thesis looks attractive.
config: Gate: reject buy when Short10 < 2.5
Scope: applied on autopilot at buy-selection time
Backtest lift: win rate 50.0% -> 66.7%, net P&L +7.75% -> +27.88%
Source: ai_portfolio_game.py buy loop; evidence scripts/backtesting/backtrack_rules.py

capital_flexibility.title: Dynamic Slot Expansion & Pyramiding
capital_flexibility.origin: Project AETHER capital-efficiency core — anti-cash-drag deployment logic.
capital_flexibility.summary: Automatically expands the maximum position-slot count by one when the cash above the profile's cash buffer exceeds 15% of equity and all slots are already full, so strong markets are not left under-deployed. Complements this with Dynamic Pyramiding — scaling additional cash into existing green winners near their breakout closes.
capital_flexibility.body: Prevents cash drag when the portfolio is fully allocated but still holding idle cash. Dynamic Slot Expansion: when cash minus the profile's cash buffer exceeds 15% of equity (system.slot_expand_free_cash) and every position slot is occupied, the maximum-positions limit is bumped by one so a fresh high-conviction candidate can still be entered rather than leaving cash uninvested. Dynamic Pyramiding: instead of only opening new names, the autopilot can add to existing winning positions trading near their recent peak closes, concentrating capital into what is already working. Both mechanisms remain bounded by the standard per-position and Scarcity-bucket caps — they deploy idle cash, they do not override the allocation ceilings.
config: Slot Expansion: (cash ratio - profile cash buffer) > 15% AND all slots full -> max_positions += 1

Dynamic Pyramiding: add idle cash to existing green winners near peak closes; only when the stop is at or above cost, and the added shares may lose at most max_trade_risk_pct (default 1%) of equity at the stop
Pyramiding guards: price must be at or above 98% of the peak close since entry (PYRAMID_PEAK_TOLERANCE, aether/scenario/steps.py); no scale-in on a symbol sold earlier the same day
Bounded: still clamped by the per-position ceiling and the Scarcity-core cap
Source: ai_portfolio_game.py slot-expansion + pyramiding blocks

drop_risk.title: Drop-Risk Flag and Size Hint
drop_risk.summary: Marks a recommended stock with 4 or more drop days (-10% or worse, not reversed the next session) in the last 3 years, the count R&D #115 tested, and gives the Oracle a size hint so that a stop-out or a worst-1% day costs the game's per-trade risk cap of the account. Advisory; nothing is blocked.

It covers the 756 sessions before the latest bar; with fewer, nothing is shown.

History says how likely a big move is, not when. R&D #117 found that skipping these buys did not help a portfolio and half-sizing them passed only on one simulated path, so this stays a warning. Junk bars in the cache still count (RS); repairing the cache is a separate job.

aether_oracle.title: AETHER Oracle (Project Oracle)
aether_oracle.summary: A read-only real-account advisory engine. Audits live holdings in the configured real account, calculates stop breaches and momentum decay, and surfaces top breakout setups toward a doubling goal set in config.
aether_oracle.origin: Project AETHER Core Team (R&D Sprints, August 2026). Decoupled read-only advisory architecture.
aether_oracle.body: The AETHER Oracle is a quantitative advisory layer. It connects to E*TRADE's production API to read the active state of the configured real account (balances and holdings). Because that account state is uncontrolled and can change at any time from manual executions, the Oracle recalculates risk parameters (trailing stops, technical decay) and recommends capital rotations each morning. It compiles a data-backed thesis, applies the AI Second-Opinion Exit Override Gate to protect breached winners, and merges it with the virtual AI-Game report into a single consolidated morning email briefing. When the account cannot be read, it renders a data-unavailable notice rather than advising on unverified balances.
config: Target: Double the configured real account by its target date (config oracle.start_equity / oracle.target_date).
Execution: Runs daily at 7:00 AM PST immediately following ai_portfolio_game.py.
Auditing: Flags CRITICAL BREACHES when current price <= technical stop loss.

Override: Seamlessly integrates the AI Second-Opinion Exit Override Gate, auditing shadow verdicts to downgrade a momentum collapse to HOLD or WATCH (sell_rules.ai_exit_override), only for a holding more than 1 ATR in profit. A stop-loss breach or a losing position is never downgraded.
Rotations: Chooses the single highest-scoring, non-overlapping bullish setup (s10 >= 2.5).

Loss filters (R&D #113, aether/buy_specs.py): an idea that gets in only through the elite-breakout waiver must be within 10% of its 52-week high, or it is held back and listed as such; an idea below a falling 200-day average is flagged. Each idea shows what was checked (Setup, scores, reward/risk) and that news, earnings and legal events were not.
Zero-Risk: Operational read-only advisory (no automated orders are placed on your brokerage).

covered_call_engine.title: Covered-Call Income Engine (R&D #26)
covered_call_engine.summary: A weekly writer that sells covered calls against risk-locked winners and books the premium to the ledger as real cash. Each option is priced with a per-symbol ATR-implied volatility, and high-conviction 'flower' winners are deliberately left uncapped so their upside stays protected.
covered_call_engine.body: The covered-call engine (aether/options.py) runs a weekly pass over open positions and writes a one-week out-of-the-money call against each risk-locked, optionable winner that has no active call, crediting the Black-Scholes-Merton premium to the ledger. If the position is still held near expiry the call is bought back (unwound) at fair value; if price closes above the strike the stock is called away at the strike. Two backtest-gated refinements (Jul-18 optimizer discipline) sit on top of the base writer. First, each premium is priced at a per-symbol implied volatility derived from the symbol's own ATR rather than a single flat 0.30 across the universe — a flat vol over-credited calm blue chips and under-credited volatile names, biasing the booked ledger. Second, winners with a strong long-term trend (Long60 at or above the configured ceiling) are excluded from writing entirely, so the engine never caps the upside of a high-conviction 'flower' — the same capital-protection instinct as Flower Protection and the ATR trailing stop.
config: Eligibility: writes only against risk-locked, optionable winners that have no active call and hold at least one 100-share contract; a call covers whole contracts only (250 shares -> 2 contracts on 200 shares), and the rest stays uncovered.
Volatility: sigma = clamp((ATR/price) x sqrt(252) x 0.67, 0.18, 0.64), calibrated by scripts/backtesting/covered_call_iv_study.py; falls back to a flat 0.30 when ATR or price is unavailable.
Flower Protection: winners with Long60 >= 6.0 (config cc_l60_ceiling / env AETHER_CC_L60_CEILING) are never written against, leaving their upside uncapped.
Pricing: European Black-Scholes-Merton, 7-day weekly expiry, risk-free rate 0.04; strike = max(1.05 x price, price + 1.5 x ATR) rounded to a $1 / $2.50 / $5 ladder by price tier.
Symmetry: the sold volatility is stored on the written call and reused at buy-to-close, so writes and unwinds price against the same model.

Expiry and settlement: the call expires on the last NYSE session on or before Friday (Thursday when Friday is a holiday) and settles on the first run after that session, at its close from Symbol_full; with no cached close it waits.
covered_call_engine.origin: Project AETHER R&D #26 (Option Trading & Volatility Patterns). Base weekly writer plus two backtest-gated refinements (per-symbol ATR-implied vol; high-conviction flower exclusion) shipped September 2026 on the covered-call follow-up (PR #60).

position_watch.title: Position Watch (concentrated holding)
position_watch.summary: A daily, recommend-only check of one concentrated holding (default INTC): TRIM a small tranche, HOLD or WAIT, with reasons, tax lots and a RETRO of the last call. Never places an order, never sells below the floor.
position_watch.origin: Built for OceanView (R&D #79): bring a concentrated position down slowly and on evidence. Rules are heuristics, reviewed against the RETRO hit rate.
position_watch.body:
Each run measures the symbol (SMA 20/50/200, drawdown from the 52-week high, 1/5/20/60-day returns), separates the sector's move from the symbol's own (beta to an equal-weight peer basket and the residual return with a z-score), checks each replacement's entry timing (stretch vs its 50-day average, RSI-14), and computes concentration against the total, including stock-plan shares and outside assets.

A TRIM needs all of: below the 50-day average, weak on its own (20-day residual z < -1), no recovery pattern forming, not a crash day, and a replacement with an OK entry. Any doubt in the inputs (stale bars, a missing peer, a failed account snapshot or live quote) turns a TRIM into WAIT; so does the day after a big drop. Suggested lots: losses first (outside the ±30-day vest/ESPP wash windows), then long-term lots with the smallest gain, short-term last.

Every call goes to a journal; the next run scores it (RETRO) and a one-line lesson can be attached.

The lots file is kept current from E*TRADE during the workbook update (aether/lots_refresh.py): it reads only the lots, uses the positions the update has just read, and changes only labels mapped in lot_sources. Nothing is written unless the lots add up to the position; the old file is backed up first. Unmapped labels (stock-plan ESPP/RSU) stay as they are. It never logs in.
config: scripts/monitoring/position_watch.py --symbol INTC [--live] (one read-only E*TRADE quote with --live)
Floor: floor_pct (default 30% of the total); tranche: tranche_pct (default 5% of the position)
Private inputs in Data/position_watch/: config (peers, replacements, vest/ESPP dates), lots, journal
Lots refresh: runs inside check_from_xls; by hand: python -m aether.lots_refresh [--write] (dry run by default); private config: "lot_sources": {"<lots label>": "<last 4>"}

invest_plan.summary: A daily check of a short, dated buy plan: which step is due, wait a day after a market drop, each holding against its stop, and the days left to the sell window. Recommend-only.
invest_plan.origin: OceanView (R&D #79): a short plan with dated steps, stops and a sell window, checked every day instead of from memory.
invest_plan.body: The plan is a private JSON file (steps with dates and amounts, rules, fills). Each day invest_plan.py says from the cached daily bars which step is due or overdue (a step counts as covered only by fills dated on or after it, within $1 or 1%), whether to wait a day because SPY fell by the plan's threshold on the last session, whether the index fund to buy is stretched, how each holding stands against its stop, and the days to the sell window.
config: scripts/monitoring/invest_plan.py (reads Data/position_watch/invest_plan.json)
Fills are recorded in the plan's fills list (date, symbol, shares, price, optional stop)

Index-fund stop: the plan's index_stop (8%) under the symbol's average cost over all fills, so a new buy moves the stop; or 1% under the confirmed support below the average cost (bars up to its last buy) when that is lower: support, but never closer than 8% and never further than 30% (index_stop_max). One SELL covers every lot of the symbol
Long-term lots: a fill with "hold": "long" counts in its symbol's average stop but never covers a dated step and is left out of the sell window (money held into the next year)

Win/loss odds per index fund (descriptive): past days in the same band of distance from the 50-day average, 20+ sessions apart, with the share up after 60 sessions, the median return, and how often -8% came before +8%
Shown on the OceanView tab when the plan file exists

harvest_list.title: Tax-Loss Harvest List
harvest_list.summary: A read-only list of every losing position across the listed E*TRADE accounts, built from the live tax lots: short- and long-term loss, the estimated tax value at your rates, wash-sale warnings and the first clean buy-back date. Recommend-only.
harvest_list.origin: OceanView year-end harvest (R&D #81, plan stage O2a): the list used to live in hand notes, where a recent buy or a lot about to turn long-term was easy to miss.
harvest_list.body: python -m aether.harvest reads each losing position's tax lots through the E*TRADE client (read-only, no login) and ranks the symbols by the tax value of selling them today. A lot is long-term once the sale date is past its one-year anniversary. A buy of the same symbol in any listed account within the last 30 days is flagged: selling only the older lots at a loss would then be partly a wash sale, so sell every lot or wait. Accounts the API doesn't list (the stock plan, a 401(k), other brokers) aren't checked. The figures are planning estimates, not tax advice.
config: python -m aether.harvest (add --json for the full list)
Tax rates: st_rate / lt_rate in Data/position_watch/config.json
Scheduled buys: acquisition_dates in Data/position_watch/config.json (vest / purchase dates of the watched symbol); a loss sale within 30 days of one is flagged with the next clean day
The watched symbol's loss lots are listed even when the whole position is up (sell them by specific lot)
Never places an order and writes nothing

rule_shadow.title: Buy Rules in Shadow
rule_shadow.summary: A rule that passed its study runs in shadow before it is wired: for every buy, the log records what the rule would have done, and a scorer later compares the names it would have held back with the ones it admitted. No decision changes.
rule_shadow.origin: Plan stage T0.4 (2026-11-23): validate a rule on PROD before it trades. The first rule in shadow is the R&D #113 loss filter, which the Oracle already applies and the game does not.
rule_shadow.body: Each game buy candidate that passes the game's own rules, and each idea the Oracle checks, gets one line in Data/rule_shadow.jsonl: date, source, symbol, price, whether the live rules admitted it, and whether the #113 loss filter would hold it back and why. aether/rule_shadow.py is the only writer (append-only, bounded, a write failure is only a warning) and holds the scorer: forward return after 5 and 20 sessions by the rule's verdict, with n. Wiring a rule still needs its pre-registered bar and two weeks or more of shadow that agree.
config: Log: Data/rule_shadow.jsonl (one writer: aether/rule_shadow.py)
Rule in shadow: R&D #113 loss filter (aether/buy_specs.py)
Scorer: rule_shadow.score(entries, closes_by_symbol)

margin_watch.title: Oracle Margin Watch
margin_watch.summary: The Oracle's daily email adds a Margin watch for every real account with a margin loan: debt, equity, the maintenance requirement, how far holdings can fall before a call, any open call as the broker states it, and the sales that free the most requirement first.
margin_watch.origin: R&D #39 Phase 1 (PR #256): the Oracle audited one account, so a margined account it doesn't trade could reach a call unseen.
margin_watch.body:
From the broker's live figures only (no live data, no section): debt and margin equity from E*TRADE's balance data, open house/Fed/minimum-equity/cash calls as stated, and the requirement from each holding's maintenance rate (a private file copied from the broker's margin page; a missing symbol is assumed at 30% and the email says how much is assumed).

Pay down first lists the five sales that free the most requirement per dollar (100% names first), losses before gains; a loss on a symbol bought in the last 30 days is marked as a wash-sale window and listed last. Holdings without prices are shown as unpriced rather than guessed. Recommend-only.
config: aether/margin_watch.py; private Data/margin_requirements.json ({last4: {SYMBOL: rate}})
Optional oracle.margin_rate_pct for the interest line
One broker read per Oracle run, shared with its audit
Pay-down for a buffer (plan O3): the deposit, or the sales at the account's average requirement, that keep a 20% / 30% fall from reaching a call

options_adviser.title: Options & Tax Adviser
options_adviser.summary: Builds a menu of protection and income strategies for a stock position (collar, protective put, covered call, cash-secured put, bull-put and bear-call spreads), each with its economics and U.S. tax considerations. Recommend-only.
options_adviser.origin: The INTC collar / CPA adviser, generalised to any holding (default symbol INTC).
options_adviser.body:
For each strategy: net cost or credit, maximum loss and gain, protection floor, upside cap and breakevens, plus tax flags (long/short-term holding period, IRC §1259 constructive sale, §1092 qualified covered call, §1091 wash sale). The engine is pure and unit-tested; the option chain comes from a saved sample by default or one read-only E*TRADE fetch with --live.

The OceanView adviser skill doesn't build this menu for employer stock under a hedging ban (the user's INTC) and uses position-watch instead; the tool itself doesn't enforce that. Tax notes are considerations, not advice.
config: python options_adviser.py --symbol SYM --print --no-email (offline sample chain)
--live: one ban-safe options_chain fetch, no browser; --dte / --expiry pick the expiry
Engine: aether/options_adviser.py; skill: .claude/commands/oceanview-adviser.md

etrade_session_safety.title: E*TRADE Session & TLS Safety
etrade_session_safety.summary: Every E*TRADE, Chaikin and EDGAR call verifies TLS certificates (against the Windows trust store when truststore is installed). A certificate failure or a token file copied from another machine never triggers an automated login.
etrade_session_safety.origin: PRs #253, #257 and #270 (2026-11): token and session calls had run with certificate checks off, and a backup copy of PROD's data brought PROD's token onto dev.
etrade_session_safety.body:
Certificates: no call turns verification off (a test scans the code for any bypass). With the optional truststore package, certificates are checked against the operating system's store, which includes a corporate or antivirus root; without it, against certifi. scripts/diagnostics/tls_precheck.py checks all three hosts before a deploy.

No login on the wrong problem: a certificate error in the token check or the renew is not a dead token, so the automated login is skipped (recorded per thread, so overlapping dashboard calls can't clear each other's note). A token file saved on another machine is ignored and doesn't trigger an automated login here; a person can still log in.
config: AETHER_TLS_TRUSTSTORE=0 falls back to certifi (verification stays on)
REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE is honoured by every call, including Chaikin's direct session
Token files record the host that saved them; another host's file is skipped

etrade_shared_login.title: Shared E*TRADE Login (opt-in)
etrade_shared_login.summary: With AETHER_ETRADE_STORE=db, PROD and dev keep one E*TRADE token and one set of renew / re-auth locks in the shared database, so a login on one machine no longer ends the other's session.
etrade_shared_login.origin: PR #268 (2026-11). PROD and dev share one E*TRADE consumer key, and on 2026-11-11/12 each machine's login killed the other's token (the stop monitor then fell back to Google prices).
etrade_shared_login.body:
One token: the token is stored as an encrypted blob (Fernet; the key is derived from the production consumer secret, which the database never sees). A machine whose token is gone loads the one the other machine minted instead of logging in, and only one machine holds the re-auth lock at a time. Lock leases use the database's clock, so two machines' clock differences don't matter. A rejected token is deleted only while the shared row still holds that token. Browser cookies stay per machine.

Outages: if the database can't be reached, each machine uses its own token file (one warning per operation) and may log in as before; after a failure the process skips the database for 5 minutes, so calls don't each wait for a connect timeout. Tokens are always mirrored to the local file. Without the opt-in nothing changes.
config: AETHER_ETRADE_STORE=db turns it on; unset = this machine's files only, as before
database.url / DATABASE_URL: the shared Postgres (reached over Tailscale from dev)
SHARED_RETRY_S = 300: after a database failure, skip it for 5 minutes
Needs the cryptography package (requirements.txt)

dev_project_model.title: Development Tab: Project Model
dev_project_model.summary: A dashboard tab that shows the AETHER services redesign (R&D #78): each step, fix and service with its status and PR, plus code metrics measured live from the source tree. Below it, every other multi-stage project with its stages, status and PR.
dev_project_model.body: The progress comes from plans/aether-services-progress.json, which each R&D #78 PR updates. The metrics are measured on every load, so they show the code as it is: lines in ai_portfolio_game.py, aether/scenario and aether/services, game.X calls and _pkg() shims in the new packages, and magic row[N] indexes. Under Other projects, each multi-stage project has its own file in plans/progress/ (goal, stages, status, PR, PROD flag, note), updated in every PR of that project. Read-only; no login needed.
config: Endpoint: GET /api/dev/project-model
Source: plans/aether-services-progress.json
Other projects: plans/progress/*.json (one file per project)

dashboard_login.title: Dashboard Login for Private Data
dashboard_login.summary: Pages and actions that show real accounts, logs or private plans, or that spend AI quota or touch E*TRADE, need the admin login. Market data and the paper game stay open.
dashboard_login.origin: PR #243 (2026-11-10); PR #252 added it to admin-only task output. The dashboard listens on the network.
dashboard_login.body: Log in at the top right with an account from web.admins; a session lasts 12 hours. The login is required for real accounts, the private plan page, the OceanView tab, logs, chat, live requalify, an AI summary on Compare, running or healing tasks, E*TRADE status and re-auth, and the output of an admin-only task. Without web.secret in the config, sessions end when the server restarts.
config: web.admins: who can log in
web.secret: signing key (set it so sessions survive a restart)
Session length: 12 hours

chaikin_session.title: Chaikin Session Renewal
chaikin_session.summary: The Chaikin login token lasts about 7 days. A daily task renews it on a weekday before it runs out, and a morning check emails a reminder when fewer than 2.5 days are left.
chaikin_session.origin: PR #251 (2026-11-10): the token kept expiring on Sunday evening, and the weekly Sunday renewal had nobody to fix a failure.
chaikin_session.body:
AETHER_Chaikin_Reauth (daily 08:00; needs a logged-on desktop because it opens Chrome) renews on a weekday when the token wouldn't outlive the next weekday run plus a day, so a Friday renews a token that would die over the weekend. At the weekend it renews only if the token dies before Monday 08:00. AETHER_Chaikin_Runway_Watch (daily 07:00) never opens a browser: it emails a reminder, at most once a day, naming the expiry time. On the System page, Check Token Runway and Login & Refresh Token run the same script (admin only).

The 08:00 renewal fills in the login and then waits up to 10 minutes for someone to click Login (or the Turnstile box), emailing once that it is waiting. Background jobs (the hourly watchdog, data fetches) never open a browser, because a headless login cannot pass Turnstile; when the session is dead they send one 'session needs a login' email at most every 6 hours.
config: Task: scripts/monitoring/chaikin_reauth.py --weekday-aware
Reminder: --notify-days 2.5
System page: --check, and --cdp --force

Shared session (opt-in, AETHER_CHAIKIN_STORE=db): the session is also kept, encrypted, in the shared database, so PROD and dev use one renewed session; session.json stays as the local copy and the newer of the two is used. python -m aether.chaikin_store --status shows both
Login wait: --login-timeout (default 600 s); alert throttle: Data/chaikin_alert_state.json (6 h)

data_completeness.title: Data Completeness Check & Reference ETFs
data_completeness.summary: Each evening the Chaikin download is compared with the sessions before it: fields that went empty, fewer snapshots, bad values, missing price bars and screen symbols that disappeared put a [DATA] banner on top of the evening email. A short list of reference ETFs is kept current every night even when they are off the screen.
data_completeness.origin: Built after the 2026-09-01 Chaikin API switch emptied 44 snapshot fields for two months unnoticed (PR #235). Reference ETFs added 2026-11-17 (PR #281) after SMH and SOXX bars stopped on 11-02 with no alarm.
data_completeness.body:
aether/data_completeness.py counts how often every snapshot field is filled and compares it with the median of the last 10 sessions; a usually-filled field that empties is an alarm, without anyone listing which fields matter. It also checks the snapshot count, value ranges (the 12-char signal string, the PGR rating) and that each stock has an OHLCV bar for the session.

Reference ETFs (default QQQ, SMH, SOXX, XLK, SPY, RSP, GDX, VXX, UVXY; VXX/UVXY stand in for the VIX index, which the data API does not serve) are fetched by the nightly repair pass as soon as they miss the latest session's bar, and the check alarms when one has no bar for the session before the checked day.
config: Run by hand: python -m aether.data_completeness [--date YYYY-MM-DD]
Reference list: rapidapi.reference_symbols in config.json (a list or "A,B") or AETHER_REFERENCE_SYMBOLS; default in aether/config.py DEFAULT_REFERENCE_SYMBOLS

preflight_buy_gate.title: Pre-Flight Buy Gate
preflight_buy_gate.summary: After a failed morning pre-flight, or when the latest data is broken (fields gone empty, missing snapshots or bars), the scheduled trade run makes no new buys, scale-ins or queued buys. Stops, exits and queued sells still run.
preflight_buy_gate.origin: PR #251 (2026-11-10): on 2026-11-09 the pre-flight failed on an expired Chaikin session, yet the 07:00 run bought on stale data. PR #259 added the log lines.
preflight_buy_gate.body:
The morning pipeline records its verdict in Data/preflight_status.json. A FAIL for today, or a record that can't be read, sets the same buy freeze the circuit breaker uses and drops queued BUY orders. A run started by hand with --run --force may still buy, and logs that it bypassed the gate. Each pre-flight logs one Pre-flight summary line naming any failed check.

Data-health freeze. The same run also checks the latest Chaikin snapshots (aether/data_completeness.py): fields that went empty, a drop in the snapshot count, bad values or missing price bars freeze new buys the same way. Only fields the game reads count (PGR rating, the four factor groups, price, signals, industry, the strength/timing counts); they are remembered in Data/data_gate_memory.json, so the freeze holds until they fill again (the check's own 10-session baseline stops alarming after about a week), and the evening email says buys are frozen while it lasts. If the newest snapshots are older than the last session, or the check cannot run, buys are frozen too. A field that stays empty for good can be released by hand: python -m aether.data_completeness --accept-fields <field> (edits only Data/data_gate_memory.json, after a backup; the game file is never touched). --force bypasses it with a [Data-Health Gate] bypassed log line.
config: Data/preflight_status.json (written by autonomous_pipeline.py)
Manual override: ai_portfolio_game.py --run --force

system_watchdog.title: System Watchdog & Alerts
system_watchdog.summary: An hourly health check: it emails on data loss, a stale backup, a missing scheduled trade run or a failing OceanView pack, reports missing scheduled tasks, and hands a pipeline crash to an AI agent for diagnosis.
system_watchdog.origin: Core infrastructure; the missed-run alert and retired tasks came in PR #259 (2026-11-13).
system_watchdog.body:
Alerts (each at most once a day): a symbol cache that loses more than 20% of its entries between runs; no successful backup for 3 days; no scheduled trade run by 07:30 PT on an NYSE session day; an OceanView context pack that failed or is more than 30 hours old. The stop monitor separately emails once a day when it has no prices for half or more of the positions it watches.

Tasks: the watchdog checks the tasks listed in scripts/utils/scheduled_tasks.json and reports missing ones, but never creates them (re-register with register_agent_tasks.ps1); tasks marked retired are left alone. Crashes: a pipeline traceback goes to an AI agent CLI, by default the Claude CLI with read-only tools, so it diagnoses rather than edits; a lock file stops repeat triggers until someone reviews it.
config: Schedule: AETHER_Watchdog, hourly
AETHER_HEALER_CMD overrides the healer command
Thresholds: cache drop 20%, backup 3 days, trade run due 07:30 PT, pack 30 h
